Nothing else changes.
claim_class: exact same-coordinate feasible-set equivalence in both integer and LP modes: 4 directional claims (source->target and target->source, each in integer and LP mode), identity projection on all 6,250 coordinates, objective relation Equal, and the identity affine inverse pairing 0<->1 (integer) and 2<->3 (LP). 575,036 obligations, all discharged by direct row reuse plus 180,000 Lin row-combinations over retained rows.
claims: Claim pair 0/1 (integer mode). Forward (source->target): all 70,633 target rows reused directly, 0 Lin steps, 101,884 obligations. Reverse (target->source): each of the 90,000 deleted rows re-derived as a Lin sum of 3-7 retained rows addressed in the target row-index space, plus 70,633 direct row refs, 90,000 Lin steps, 191,884 obligations.
Claim pair 2/3 (LP mode): identical structure with integrality obligations removed (95,634 / 185,634 obligations); the 90,000-step list of block 3 is byte-identical to block 1 (14,992,979 B each).

Each Return repeats the per-variable ladder: 6,250 VarLower + 6,250 VarUpper refs (+6,250 'Exact' VarInt in integer mode), one ref per output row, the objective Equal, 6,250 projection identities and 6,250 inverse identities, all in docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:229 order.

Deleted-row witnesses are paths over retained rows only, length 3:33,075, 4:11,051, 5:30,705, 6:8,949, 7:6,220; each telescopes to the deleted row's exact expression with RHS 0 and every multiplier 1.

Claim spec keys: reverse, input_integers, output_integers, objective Equal, projection (6,250 identity pairs), inverse (u32 index of the opposing claim).

Only step kind used is Lin: step 0 of block 1 = {'Lin':{'id':0,'kind':'Le','constant':'0','terms':[[{'RowUpper':6258},'1'],[{'RowUpper':3136},'1'],[{'RowUpper':135},'1']]}}; 394,188 terms per reverse block.

agent_manual_work: Wrote a section-aware exact MPS parser (fractions.Fraction for every coefficient, RHS, bound; unsupported constructs rejected), then a second independent field-position reader in output/verify.py because numeric fields exceed classic fixed-MPS width, and had to reconcile the two tokenizations by hand.

Classified all 160,633 rows (8 capacity rows c1-c8 RHS 2,144,000, coefficient sums 12,557,026-13,109,876; 160,625 rows with one +1 and one -1 and RHS 0) and computed 6,250 singleton SCCs, a Kahn topological order and the DAG transitive reduction with hand-written Python - the graph package was absent (ModuleNotFoundError: networkx).

Proved equality of full original and reduced reachability with Python-int bitsets, checked that no retained edge has an alternate retained path, and tested four further hypotheses (capacity redundancy from bounds, SCC-based variable identification, independent graph blocks, forced-zero closure: 6,250 principal closures, 1,624,375 edge checks).

Built 90,000 retained-row path certificates with exact telescoping coefficient and RHS checks, then wrote output/verify.py (185 lines) which re-parses both MPS files, verifies the row-set difference is exactly the certificate set, re-walks every path and re-runs Kahn + bitset reachability.

Produced the deletion-only MPS by copying source lines verbatim while dropping 90,000 ROWS and 180,000 COLUMNS records, plus audit.json (10,928,614 B) with the 90,000 certificates and SHA-256 of both files (f2a54bdd..., 7cd91dfc...).

friction: No proof-construction API: 180,000 Lin steps, 575,036 obligations and the two 18 MB blocks are emitted by Python string building; the only kernel-facing writing tool is rpx assemble, which takes finished RPA text.

Every Lin ref must be an index in its claim's input model, and deletion rebases indices: retained row c7002 is index 7001 in source but 6773 in target (228 earlier deletions), while the finding names rows in source order in audit.json - the mapping is rebuilt by re-parsing the target MPS and matching on names only (tools/prepare_affine.py:133).

The target model is an artifact written outside the toolchain: run() globs the run output directory for exactly one .mps (tools/prepare_affine.py:154) and asserts it, so target identity, provenance and the retained index space live in the run dir rather than in a structured edit.

The same 90,000-step derivation set is emitted twice because one Block per claim cannot reference another: 29.99 MB of the 40.84 MB RPA is an exact duplicate, and a 6,250-entry variable obligation ladder is regenerated four times.

Resource verdicts are unattributable: the same rpa/request bytes gave exit 3 RESOURCE_LIMIT ('proof work budget', no location) on kernel cc96f69d and exit 0 (work 10,759,860) on kernel c699e384, so a compiler cannot tell a too-large proof from an inefficient verifier.

top_capability: RULE_BUILDERS - a batch Lin row-combination builder with precondition checks, which would own the 180,000 steps (90,000 per domain mode, each an exact sum of 3-7 retained rows) that are this certificate's entire mathematical content, and with it the target-construction and claim-ladder capabilities that surround those combinations.
notes: Deletion-only reformulation: variables, domains, integer markers, objective, RHS, senses and retained coefficients are untouched, so the proof's only content is the 90,000 row-combinations plus the claim ladder. Scale: rpa 40,840,280 B = 15.2% of the 256 MiB text limit, rpx 27,989,684 B, request 291,564 B, work 10,759,860 = 1.1% of the default 1e9 budget, peak_live_facts 90,000, branches 0, execute 1.234 s - MULTI_PART_ASSEMBLY is not exercised and the lift/point machinery (Flow/Interval/Menu/Cases/Signed, points, bijections) is unused. Row deletion needs nothing mutable on the model side: the immutable source only has to supply row identity and exact row expressions (plus the re-based index map of the derived target), which is why MODEL_READBACK and EDIT_AUDIT-shaped provenance are the two things a row-deletion claim asks of it. The agent's own output/verify.py is the only oracle this case had; it duplicates an MPS reader, a telescoping check and a Kahn/bitset reachability sweep that the compiler layer would have to own.
